answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Each gets the Voting card set with that color on its backs and keeps their own Ambush card; remove cards that target colors not playing. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: ID card upright in its plastic stand; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down.

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed; once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: choices may change until revealed; reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: No. Red is the Target because Red has the most votes (three), even though three is not a majority of all seven players. The rule is most votes; no four-vote majority is required.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to any other applicable Ambush rule.
answers.evidence: Vote: if several players tie for most votes, all are Targets; with tied Targets, voting for any one satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep a player alive; every non-Target who did not vote for any Target is eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception.
answers.evidence: Vote: every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated; successful Ambush is an exception.

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count as one, so Red and Yellow tie for the most counted votes and are both Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red survives and may eliminate only a player who voted for Red, namely Yellow. Yellow is eliminated; Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives. The survivors are Red and Pink.
answers.evidence: Ambush example: Red and Yellow tie at one vote each; Red can retaliate only against Yellow; Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets the Target choose exactly one player who voted for them to eliminate, not all four voters. They also may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: chooses “one of the players who voted for them”; cannot choose someone who voted for a different Target.

answers.answer: The Ambush fails, and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another Conspire and vote, and only the surviving players participate in subsequent votes.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: three or more survivors continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are not four points: each card has a value of 3, 4, or 5 points, so the total depends on the cards' values.
answers.evidence: One survivor collects all four central Gold Bars; Gold Bars are cards whose values are 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of three cards—Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go—may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; choose face down; reveal simultaneously when both are ready.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar under this outcome, including those eliminated in it. Nobody takes the four central bars: leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: No survivors: each player not participating in final vote gets one deck bar; leave four central bars for next round and add no new bars.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Share: you get 2 and opponent gets 2.

answers.answer: The finalist who chose Share gets zero central bars; the finalist who chose Steal gets all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Steal: Share player gets 0; Steal player gets 4.

answers.answer: The finalist who chose Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist who chose Steal gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table and rule: Grab One & Go against Steal gives its player 1 and the opponent 3.

answers.answer: The finalist who chose Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist who chose Share gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table and rule: Grab One & Go against Share gives its player 1 and the opponent 3.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar; two bars remain central. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool to four.
answers.evidence: Both Grab One & Go: each receives one; leave two in center and add just two new bars for next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Both Steal: neither finalist receives gold; everyone outside the pair gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of the round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: end-of-round check after awards; 25 points with 6–9 players, 24 with 10–12; highest point total wins.

answers.answer: For exactly two tied qualifying leaders at game end, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total; one extra Showdown does not end the tie if the highest totals remain tied. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round: stand all Player ID cards upright for the next round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary; if no winner, everyone returns and IDs are stood upright.

answers.answer: Before every vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, and texting. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: “roughly a minute and a half at most”; any communication method; game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID whom you want to target, and place it face down in front of yourself. To defend yourself when you suspect you are the target, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; use the card matching target's ID color; use Ambush to defend yourself.

answers.answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: Vote: knock down eliminated players' ID cards and leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.

answers.answer: After checking for a winner, if play continues and the entire pot was awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden. The next central pool is four bars.
answers.evidence: If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars; new central bars are dealt face down.

answers.answer: No. Blue remains the Target because Blue has the most counted votes; a successful Ambush protects Blue but does not change which player received the most votes or make Purple a Target. Purple is not a Target on the stated tally of four votes for Blue and three for Purple. Voters for Purple do not survive merely because Blue's Ambush succeeds: they did not vote for a Target, so they are eliminated unless protected by their own successful Ambush.
answers.evidence: Vote: most votes determines Target; every other player who did not vote for any Target is eliminated, subject to Ambush. Ambush: successful protection does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.

answers.answer: The booklet's stated instruction is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown and repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. However, it does not specify how to arrange or conduct a Showdown when more than two players (here, three) are tied; that procedure is unsupported and requires publisher clarification.
answers.evidence: Scoring: repeat Showdowns as necessary; source limitation says card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players and provide no arrangement for three or more tied leaders.

answers.answer: Yes. In an extra Showdown where both tied finalists Steal, each receives zero gold and every player outside the pair gets one bar from the deck. The resulting point totals are compared across all players, so an outside player could become the winner if that reward gives them the single highest total.
answers.evidence: Scoring: compare totals of all players after each extra Showdown; outside double-Steal reward can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.
